title: Big O Notation
definition: Big O defines the upper bound of an algorithm's complexity. It describes the worst-case scenario for how the runtime or space requirements grow as the input size (N) grows towards infinity.
simpleExplanation: If I give you 10 times more work, will it take you 10 times longer (O(N)), 100 times longer (O(N^2)), or the exact same amount of time (O(1))?
terminalOutput:
O(1) - Constant
O(log N) - Logarithmic (Binary Search)
O(N) - Linear (Simple Loop)
O(N log N) - Linearithmic (Merge Sort)
O(N^2) - Quadratic (Nested Loops)
O(2^N) - Exponential (Recursive Fibonacci)

answers.question: **Basic:** Write a function to implement the core logic of Big O.
**Intermediate 1:** Optimize Big O to handle edge cases like empty arrays or negative numbers.
**Intermediate 2:** Solve a standard interview variation of Big O (e.g. LeetCode Medium).
**Advanced:** Scale Big O for massive datasets or implement it recursively.
**Expert/FAANG:** Solve Big O in O(1) space or O(N) time when constraints are extremely tight.
